## 1 - Collect, then normalize
Three sources, fetched **in parallel** off one trigger and joined by a 3-input Merge, so a run costs the slowest source rather than the sum of all three.

Every fetch gets **3 attempts** and then **continues on error**: a dead source becomes an error-level data quality warning and a report marked `partial`, not a red execution and an empty dashboard.

A source that answers with nothing is reported as **unknown, not zero**. "0 active projects" is a measurement; what happened is that nobody measured, and the dashboard says which system did not answer.

## 2 - Calculate, then think
Every figure is computed here, in code. Claude receives the finished numbers, their prior-period comparisons, the per-team breakdowns and a bucketed series across the window - never the 314 raw rows. It interprets; it is never asked to count.

**Report Changed?** compares a fingerprint of the *computed figures* against the last published run. Unchanged means no model call and no writes: the run stops at **Nothing To Update** and the existing report is left exactly as it is.

**Any Data To Report?** short-circuits when every source is dead, so the model is never paid to analyse nothing.

## 3 - Validate, then publish
Nothing the model writes reaches the dashboard unchecked. Every number in its prose is matched against the figures it was given; unverified ones are named on the page and the confidence badge is forced down, whatever confidence the model claimed for itself.

One RPC - `publish_report()` - writes the whole report in **one transaction**: run, metrics, breakdowns, insights, data quality and the cleaned records. It commits everything or nothing, and it **deletes** the run's old child rows rather than merging into them, so a re-run cannot leave a stale warning behind.

`run_id = run_<period>_<start>_<end>_<reference date>` - derived from the window, never from the clock and never from an execution id. Running this ten times on unchanged data rewrites the same row ten times: **one report per period**, not a pile of versions to choose between.

n8n writes with the **secret** key (`service_role`) held in a credential. The dashboard reads with the **publishable** key (`anon`) under RLS that grants SELECT and nothing else - and grants nothing at all on `people_records`.
